PullRequest.Title: layout: backport primary side bar width fix to 1.137
PullRequest.Body:
Backports #334864 to `release/1.137`.

## Changes

- Preserve the user-set primary side bar width when toggling it with the side bar on the right.
- Redistribute split-view changes according to layout priority.
- Add a regression test covering #334167.

## Validation

- `npm run hygiene`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/base/test/browser/ui/splitview/splitview.test.ts` — 19 passing

## Local environment notes

- `npm run compile-client` was attempted but the worktree lacks the unrelated built-in extension dependency `@vscode/markdown-editor`.
- `npm run typecheck-client` was attempted but the worktree lacks the unrelated runtime type dependencies `original-fs` and `electron`.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle the primary side bar on the right while floating panels are enabled, causing the activity bar's fixed-width constraint to change synchronously during visibility propagation.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: WorkbenchLayout.setSideBarHidden calls Grid.setViewVisible; BranchNode/SplitView.setViewVisible invokes the part visibility path; ActivitybarPart fires onDidChange; SplitView.onViewChange clamps the fixed width, computes priority order, and calls the same relayout/resize/distribute/layoutViews sequence as before. The outer visibility operation then completes its existing distribute/layout pass. All work is synchronous on the UI critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronous IView.layout calls for each direct child plus sash and scrollable-element layout updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One child-layout pass from the constraint-change relayout, covering the containing branch's direct children; the workbench middle branch has at most five direct children. The surrounding visibility operation already performs its own existing pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same onDidChange handler called relayout([index]), which executed resize, distributeEmptySpace, layoutViews, sash updates, and scrollable-element updates once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These calls must finish before the side bar toggle completes, but their count is unchanged by the diff; only resize priority order changes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Direct children in the affected split view after grid grouping, not all descendants. The concrete workbench middle branch contains up to activity bar, primary side bar, editor, panel, and auxiliary bar (effective cardinality at most five).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully serialized and re-entrant on the UI thread; no queue, limiter, coalescer, worker, or parallel work is involved. The diff does not change the number of relayout passes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache, cache key, negative cache, or cold/warm distinction exists on this path; visible-size state and proportions are existing per-view layout state and the diff does not change their lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the synchronous call path and unchanged layout-pass count from the traced event wiring, SplitView implementation, grid descriptor, and regression test.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Individual child layout cost depends on active editor and view contents, but both pre- and post-diff execute the same child-layout cardinality, so that uncertainty does not establish an added performance cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The added range/filter allocations and priority reordering are bounded by a tiny direct-child set in this product scenario and do not add a layout pass or expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: A generic SplitView or nested Grid view changes minimum/maximum size, priority, or snap constraints through IView.onDidChange.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The event synchronously enters SplitView.onViewChange, clamps the requested/current size, computes sibling priority arrays, and performs relayout. Before the diff it entered the same relayout path with only the changed index marked low priority; after the diff the resize order accounts for all Low/High siblings. layoutViews still invokes every direct child once.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Layout every direct child view and update sashes/scroll dimensions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one call per direct child for each constraint event, unchanged by the diff. Nested grid propagation can trigger one such pass per ancestor branch, also unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: onViewChange already called relayout, which performed collection-wide resize, empty-space distribution, child layout, sash enablement, and scroll updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous UI work blocks completion of the constraint event, but the patch changes redistribution order rather than the number of view layout calls.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of direct sibling views per split and nesting depth after grid grouping. New range/filter work is linear for normal-priority siblings; pushToStart/pushToEnd can reorder priority entries quadratically in the number of priority-marked direct siblings, but realistic large pane/editor collections do not establish many such marked siblings, while the workbench priority-bearing branch is bounded to five.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single-threaded and serialized per event. Events are not coalesced before or after the diff, and the patch adds no concurrency or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No memoization or external cache is consulted. Existing proportional-size state is saved after relayout in both versions; the diff neither invalidates nor retains additional long-lived cache entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the patch adds transient array scans but no additional relayout, rendering boundary, retained state, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Custom embedders could theoretically construct unusually wide split views with many priority-marked children, but repository call sites do not establish a realistic hot trigger at that cardinality, and existing relayout/layout work already scales across all direct children.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence actionable regression. The transient bookkeeping is minor relative to the unchanged collection-wide layout pass, and no realistic repository scenario proves harmful scaling or user-visible latency.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff. Traced the synchronous side-bar visibility/constraint path and generic split/grid constraint propagation, including direct-child cardinality, nested layout behavior, transient allocations, cache state, and expensive-boundary/concurrency behavior. No diff-introduced performance finding met the reporting threshold.
